title: Two requests' DFlash2 verify on the Q5 tensor-core route on the RTX 5090: pair rounds 37.1 to 22.7 ms, 420.86 tok/s against shipped 388.42; kept by rule
question: EXP-081's fork DFlash2 decodes one request faster than shipped and upstream, but a pair of requests ran 37.1 ms rounds (269.17 tok/s together) against upstream DFlash2's 22.0-22.4 ms (453.95 tok/s) and shipped MTP3's pair at 388.42 tok/s. Is the excess the 16-column verify leaving the fork's Q5 tensor-core route, and with 16 columns on it, how much of the gap closes while MTP3 stays byte-identical?
answer: Almost all of it. Two requests' K=7 verify is 16 columns, and the fork's Q5 small-T tensor-core route (EXP-057, EXP-077) accepted only 4 and 8, so the MLP-down, GDN value/z and attention gate/value Q5 projections ran on SIMT row kernels in a two-request round while a one-request round kept them on the tensor cores. With the route extended to 16 columns (spike 7e4d120a: a second m16n8k16 MMA per k16 step, two pipeline stages), a pair decoded 420.86 tok/s together (223.86 and 220.97 each) in 22.7 ms rounds: 8.4% above shipped MTP3's pair and 56.4% above EXP-079/081's port, 7.3% below upstream DFlash2's pair, whose rounds took 22.0-22.4 ms. That closes 97% of the round gap to upstream; the rest of upstream's lead is tokens per round on different outputs (5.02-5.10 against 5.22-5.63). A lone request on the same server decoded 369.64 tok/s. MTP3 on the binary answered 89/89 role-corpus cases byte-identically to shipped, and every op test and the DFlash2 real-model test at one and two requests passed.

decision.rule: Pre-registered before the window (PLAN.md): keep the route if every GPU test passes, spk3-mtp3-c1 answers 89/89 byte-identically to the shipped run, there are no DFlash2 request errors and the pair's mean round is <= 33.0 ms (at least a quarter of EXP-081's 14.9 ms gap to upstream closed); reject on a test failure, broken MTP3 identity, a request error or a pair round > 33.0 ms. Reported beside the rule: the share of the gap closed, the pair against shipped 388.42 and upstream 453.95 tok/s, and the remaining round attributed by kernel from the trace.
decision.reason: The fork's own tensor-core route, extended by one MMA tile, brings two-request DFlash2 rounds to upstream's and the pair past shipped MTP3's, without moving an MTP3 output byte.
decision.not_decided_here: Adoption, as in EXP-081: the spike still refuses durable checkpoints with DFlash2, BF16 KV leaves two device state slots at two requests (NVFP4 KV, EXP-080, was measured on upstream only), and DFlash2's outputs have had one unpowered screen. The trace was captured but not attributed: the remaining 0.3-0.7 ms per round against upstream is smaller than the outputs' tokens-per-round difference.
decision.next: Carry DFlash2's context ring through checkpoints, fanout and restore on the spike, so a DFlash2 profile can keep the durable store; then measure the two-request profile with NVFP4 KV and four device state slots, and run a powered quality screen against the shipped MTP3 profile.

method.appliance: RTX 5090 (32,607 MiB), Windows 11, Docker Desktop, WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04; one arm at a time on 127.0.0.1:18099 with production stopped
method.window: Windows lane hold taken at about 01:09Z; the driver (exp082-window.sh) ran detached on the appliance: dead-man armed 01:09:11Z, production stopped 01:09:16Z, restored healthy 01:21:38Z (742 s down), dead-man cancelled, the arms' checkpoint roots removed, the trace exported after the restore; the hold was released at about 01:23Z with production /health 200 from WSL and from Windows. Production had served no request since EXP-081's window.

runtime.source: spike/dflash2-5090 at 7e4d120a025eac2a5898acb0d3a4006801e5fd1c: EXP-081's 28a1abe6, its ledger 2338f5cc, and 7e4d120a, which lets the Q5 small-T tensor-core kernel take 16 columns and routes 16 columns to it in the Q5 linear-add row split (MLP down at K=17408), the GDN value/z projection and the attention gate/value projection. Per-column arithmetic is unchanged, so column j of a 16-column pass equals column j mod 8 of an 8-column pass over the same tokens.

limits: One pair run per arm; the pair's tokens per round depend on its two outputs, so aggregate rates mix route cost with drafting.
The upstream and shipped pairs are EXP-078's runs on this appliance, not reruns in this window.
The trace was captured but not attributed, so the remaining per-round difference to upstream is unexplained by kernel.
The spike binary is an incremental archive build (source_dirty=true) of a branch, not a release candidate, and still refuses durable checkpoints with DFlash2.

MTP3 identity is shown on the corpus only. The route also applies to prefill pieces of exactly 16 tokens, which capture and rewrite frontiers can cut; whether any corpus request cut such a piece is not recorded.
